--- execute: warning: false knitr: opts_knit: global.par: true opts_chunk: comment: '' fig.width: 5.5 fig.height: 5.5 out.width: 80% --- # Introduction to **rtemis.draw** {#sec-rtemisdraw} **`rtemis.draw`** is a plotting package from the [rtemis](https://rtemis.org) project. Like **`plotly`** (@sec-plotly), it produces interactive [htmlwidgets](https://www.htmlwidgets.org), but it provides data-first `draw_*()` functions that take plain vectors, lists, or data frames and choose sensible defaults, so most plots take a single call. Charts are rendered with [Apache ECharts](https://echarts.apache.org), and automatically follow the light or dark theme of the page they are displayed in. ::: callout-note `rtemis.draw` is available from [R-universe](https://rtemis-org.r-universe.dev) and is currently under review for CRAN. ::: Full documentation is available at [docs.rtemis.org](https://docs.rtemis.org/r/draw/). ## Setup ### Installation Until the package is released on CRAN, install it from R-universe: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} install.packages( "rtemis.draw", repos = c("https://rtemis-org.r-universe.dev", "https://cloud.r-project.org") ) ``` ::: ### Libraries Load libraries we will be using in this chapter: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} library(rtemis.draw) library(data.table) options(datatable.print.class = TRUE) ``` ::: ### Synthetic Data We use the same synthetic dataset as in the previous two chapters: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} set.seed(2022) dt <- data.table( PID = sample(8001:9000, size = 100), Age = rnorm(100, mean = 33, sd = 8), Weight = rnorm(100, mean = 70, sd = 9), SysBP = rnorm(100, mean = 110, sd = 6), DiaBP = rnorm(100, mean = 80, sd = 6), Sex = factor(sample(c("Female", "Male"), size = 100, replace = TRUE)) ) dt[, SysBP := SysBP + 0.5 * Age] dt[Sex == "Male", Weight := Weight + rnorm(.N, mean = 16, sd = 1.5)] dt[Sex == "Male", Age := Age + rnorm(.N, mean = 6, sd = 1.8)] ``` ::: Define a color palette `palette`. Unlike in the previous chapters, we do not need a separate semi-transparent version of the palette: functions that fill areas, like `draw_histogram()` and `draw_density()`, have a `fill_alpha` argument, which is automatically set depending on whether there are multiple groups or not, but can be overridden if desired. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} palette <- c("#43A4AC", "#FA9860") ``` ::: ::: callout-note All `draw_*()` functions share a common set of arguments: `title`, `xlab`, `ylab`, `theme`, `width`, `height`, `palette`, and `filename`. If `palette` is not specified, the rtemis palette is used. ::: ## Box plot `draw_boxplot()` accepts a numeric vector, a list of numeric vectors, or a data frame of numeric columns, and draws one box per element or column. Unlike **`ggplot2`**, there is no need to convert to long format first. Unlike **`plotly`**, there is no need to add each box one at a time. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} draw_boxplot(dt[, .(SysBP, DiaBP)]) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: Use `palette` to specify the colors and `labels` to specify the box labels: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} draw_boxplot( dt[, .(SysBP, DiaBP)], palette = palette, labels = c("Systolic BP", "Diastolic BP") ) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: ### Grouped boxplot Use `group` to split a vector by a factor: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} draw_boxplot(dt[, Age], group = dt[, Sex], palette = palette[2:1]) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: ## Histogram ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} draw_histogram(dt[, Age], palette = palette[1]) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: We can specify the number of bins with `breaks`, and axis labels with `xlab` and `ylab`: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} draw_histogram( dt[, Age], breaks = 24, palette = palette[1], xlab = "Age (years)" ) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: ### Grouped Histogram ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} draw_histogram( dt[, Age], group = dt[, Sex], palette = palette[2:1] ) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: `bar_mode` controls the placement of the groups' bars within each bin: `"group"` (the default) places them side by side, whereas `"stack"` stacks them vertically. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} draw_histogram( dt[, Age], group = dt[, Sex], breaks = 24, bar_mode = "stack", palette = palette[2:1] ) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: ## Density plot `draw_density()` estimates the density internally with `stats::density()`, so there is no need to compute and pass the coordinates ourselves as with **`plotly`**. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} draw_density(dt[, Age], palette = palette[1]) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: ### Grouped density plot ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} draw_density(dt[, Age], group = dt[, Sex], palette = palette[2:1]) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: ## Barplot ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} schools <- data.frame(UCSF = 4, Stanford = 7, Penn = 12) ``` ::: `draw_bar()` takes the category labels as `x` and the bar heights as `y`. No data frame or explicit factor is needed; the bars appear in the order provided: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} draw_bar( names(schools), as.numeric(schools[1, ]), palette = palette[1], ylab = "N schools" ) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: ## Scatterplot ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} draw_scatter(dt[, Age], dt[, SysBP], xlab = "Age", ylab = "SysBP", palette = palette[1]) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: Pass `fit = "gam"` (or `"glm"`) to overlay a fitted line and 95% confidence band: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} draw_scatter( dt[, Age], dt[, SysBP], fit = "gam", xlab = "Age", ylab = "SysBP", palette = palette[1] ) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: ### Grouped Scatterplot ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} draw_scatter( dt[, Age], dt[, SysBP], group = dt[, Sex], xlab = "Age", ylab = "SysBP", palette = palette[2:1] ) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: With a grouping variable, `fit` draws a separate fitted line for each group: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} draw_scatter( dt[, Age], dt[, SysBP], group = dt[, Sex], fit = "gam", xlab = "Age", ylab = "SysBP", palette = palette[2:1] ) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: ## Themes Charts follow the page theme (light or dark) by default. To force a theme, pass one to the `theme` argument: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} draw_scatter(dt[, Age], dt[, SysBP], theme = theme_dark()) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: ## Save plot to file We'll use the grouped boxplot example from above to show how to save a plot to file. Pass an `.svg` `filename` to any `draw_*()` function, or call `save_drawing()` on an existing widget. SVG export requires [Node.js](https://nodejs.org). ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} p <- draw_boxplot(dt[, Age], group = dt[, Sex], palette = palette[2:1]) save_drawing(p, "Age_by_Sex_rtemis.draw.svg", width = 550, height = 550) ``` ::: or directly: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} draw_boxplot( dt[, Age], group = dt[, Sex], palette = palette[2:1], filename = "Age_by_Sex_rtemis.draw.svg" ) ``` ::: ## See also - Base R Graphics ([@sec-basegraphics]) - Introduction to **ggplot2** ([@sec-ggplot2]) - Introduction to **plotly** ([@sec-plotly]) ## Resources - [rtemis.draw Documentation](https://docs.rtemis.org/r/draw/)
